assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural empirical industrial organization has fundamentally changed how economists measure demand, competition, and policy counterfactuals.
assessment.attribution: Pakes, Berry, and Bresnahan are central architects of the econometric and economic framework, though the listed contribution reflects an unusually broad research community.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been extensively used across industries and have demonstrated durable practical and scientific influence.
uncertainties: Credit allocation is difficult because several additional listed researchers made essential contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The firm-heterogeneity framework transformed modern trade theory and empirical analysis of trade, productivity, and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the defining selection framework, while Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: Its implications have been tested widely and are now a standard basis for quantitative trade research.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit between the core model and its later extensions remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on management practices established organizational quality as a measurable and consequential determinant of productivity and economic performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen developed the central measurement and research program, with Sadun a major contributor to evidence on management and organizations.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated across countries, firms, and policy-relevant settings over a substantial period.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation and portability of management-practice measures remain active empirical questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative trade models made the gains from trade and the distributional consequences of trade policy more rigorously measurable.
assessment.attribution: Kortum's work is foundational to modern quantitative trade, while Costinot and Rodriguez-Clare made influential contributions to its welfare and measurement toolkit.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply embedded in current trade analysis and has generated a large empirical literature.
uncertainties: This is a cumulative program with substantial antecedents and overlapping contributions beyond the proposed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods gave applied economists a tractable way to estimate forward-looking decisions and conduct policy counterfactuals.
assessment.attribution: Rust provided the seminal framework; Keane and Eckstein made important methodological and applied advances in dynamic structural modeling.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been influential for decades in labor, industrial organization, transportation, and related fields.
uncertainties: The scope of credit is broad, and computational and identification limitations can affect applied conclusions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical and empirical work on adverse selection substantially improved understanding of insurance-market failures and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Salanie helped establish the theoretical and econometric approach, while Finkelstein and Einav produced especially influential empirical evidence and methods.
assessment.maturity: A large body of subsequent work has applied and refined these insights in health, auto, and other insurance markets.
uncertainties: Evidence on the prevalence and welfare importance of selection varies across insurance settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Economic analysis of information goods, network effects, compatibility, and digital-market competition has had exceptional intellectual and policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Shapiro, Varian, and Farrell made foundational contributions to the analytical framework for network and technology markets.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have endured through multiple technological waves and underpin a major modern industrial-organization literature.
uncertainties: The contribution combines interconnected strands, making a single prize citation and complete credit allocation challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental market and strategic-behavior research supplied influential evidence on how institutions and bounded reasoning shape economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Plott and Holt developed foundational experimental-market traditions, while Camerer made central contributions to behavioral game theory and experimental economics.
assessment.maturity: The experimental approach is mature, widely replicated, and integrated into mainstream economic research.
uncertainties: Laboratory external validity and the allocation of credit among several foundational experimental researchers remain debated.
